syntax_clues_detected: f86v4.1 through f86v4.4 are @Cc type — Central Circle labels. These four long text lines run INSIDE or immediately encircling the large central circular/medallion illustration at the top-center of the folio. The @Cc type indicates text that wraps around or is inscribed within the boundary of that circular drawing.

f86v4.5 has ONE <-> marker: 'pcheodar.oedy.qokeol.qoeol<->oqokeol.dar.ol.olair.am' — bisected by a vertical or organic element descending from the upper-right fish/creature illustration, most likely a tail fin or tentacle extension crossing the text zone at that point.

f86v3.15 has ONE <-> marker: 'tshdshey.dalkshdy.shocfhy.saiin.or.airody<->chedaly' — bisected by a body element of the lower-left creature/organism illustration (likely its connecting tube, trunk, or limb crossing from left to right through the text region).

f86v3.16 has ONE <-> marker: 'dcheody.skeeody.qokshey.cheodain.ykched<->saraldy' — same bisecting element as f86v3.15, the body/tube of the lower-left biological figure cuts horizontally through this adjacent line.

f86v3.18 has ONE <-> marker: 'pchedaiin.dchedy.qokchdy.qopchol.shol<->sheody.solkam' — bisected again by the same lower-left organic structure, confirming the biological figure's body span crosses at least three consecutive text lines (3.15, 3.16, 3.18).

f86v6 section ($P=O, $I=T): all 45 lines are plain +P0 paragraph continuation — the large right-margin vertical text column. No bisection markers. This block flows along the right edge, rotating 90 degrees (written sideways) relative to the main folio axis.
f86v5 section ($P=P, $I=T): 39 lines all +P0 / +Pr — the left-margin vertical text column. No bisection markers. Also written sideways along the left margin.

f86v3 section ($P=Q, $I=C): mixed @Pb / +Pb (probable 'b' block type, a secondary paragraph block) and @P0 / +P0 lines. Contains the three <-> bisection events at lines 3.15, 3.16, 3.18. The @Pb sub-blocks (lines 3.1–3.14 and 3.23–3.36) bracket the bisection zone.
f86v4 section ($P=N, $I=C): the central circle (@Cc) block plus a short paragraph (5 lines, @P0/+P0/+Pc) that has the lone bisection at line 4.5.
NO @Lp, @Ls, or @L0 isolated label loci present anywhere in f86v — no individual plant/star labels of that type on this folio.
Folio page number visible in lower-right margin: '129' in pencil (modern addition, not Voynich script).

Body is teardrop or seed-shaped, covered in overlapping curved scale-plates (like pine cone or artichoke). Color: body scales outlined in medium warm brown (~#8B5E3C), interior parchment cream-tan; small blue accent pigment touches visible on upper scales (~#6A8FA0 pale blue-grey). Tail or root structure fans outward below-right in thin curved lines. Approximate position: upper-left of folio.

upper_right_creature: large biological/zoomorphic figure in upper-right quadrant, symmetric partner to upper-left creature. Same scale-plate body morphology, slightly different orientation — head/aperture faces lower-left. Color: same warm brown ink (~#8B5E3C), blue accent touches on upper scale nodes. A long tapered 'beak' or 'snout' extension projects leftward toward the center, potentially the element causing the bisection at f86v4.5. Background behind creature has faint ruled or wavy lines suggesting water or atmosphere.

upper_center_text_medallion: the oval/circular zone in the upper-center of the folio containing the @Cc text block (f86v4.1–4.4). Not a drawn circle per se but a functional text zone defined by where the two upper creatures' bodies leave open space. This zone is filled with dense Voynich script in four long sweeping lines. Background: raw parchment (~#E8D5A0 cream), slightly aged yellow-brown. The text curves slightly suggesting the scribe was aware of the surrounding illustrations.

Contains faint pencil-like lines suggesting a botanical or biological sketch that was never fully inked. Possibly two elongated leaf or pod shapes at oblique angles. Body is elongated, tubular, with a heavily textured scaly exterior — scales appear as overlapping teardrop shapes in rows, rendered in brown ink. Head/aperture at top-right of the figure; tail or root base fans at lower-left with frilled or ruffled lobes. Blue pigment accents visible on scales across the mid-body band (~#5A8090 steel blue-grey). This creature's body tube crosses horizontally through the text at f86v3.15, 3.16, and 3.18, creating the <-> bisection events. The figure's position spans approximately x=60–380, y=760–980 normalized.

lower_right_creature: large biological figure in lower-right quadrant, symmetric partner to lower_left_creature. Same morphology: scaly tubular body, frill/lobe base, aperture at top-left. right_margin_text_column: the block of text (f86v6, 45 lines) running vertically along the right margin of the folio, written rotated 90° clockwise so it reads from bottom to top when the folio is held normally. The page number '129' in the lower right confirms this is the verso side. The inverted text occupies y=840–1000 normalized.

parchment_background: aged parchment, color ~#E2CC95 warm cream-yellow, with subtle age spots, foxing, and water staining visible especially along left margin and bottom edge. The right binding margin shows a narrow strip of deeper tan (#C4A870) where the folio meets the gutter.

upper_left_creature.description: A large zoomorphic or biological figure occupying the upper-left quadrant of the folio. The body is roughly oval or teardrop-shaped, tapering to a fan of curved tail/root filaments in the lower-right direction. The surface is covered in dense overlapping curved scale-plates arranged in concentric diagonal rows, evoking a pine cone, artichoke, or feathered body. The aperture or 'head' opening faces lower-right, slightly toward the page center. Rendered in confident brown-sepia ink outline with no fill wash — the interior remains parchment cream. Notable blue-grey pigment touches (~#6A8FA0) accent the tips of approximately 8–12 upper-center scales, distinguishing this feature from the purely ink-drawn lower scales. The fanned tail filaments below the body are thin curved lines in lighter ink, spreading rightward in an arc.

color.blue_accent_touches: pale steel blue-grey, ~#6A8FA0, applied as small dots or short strokes on select upper scale tips
color.tail_filaments: slightly lighter warm brown, ~#A07848, thinner line weight than body outline

upper_right_creature.description: A large zoomorphic figure in the upper-right quadrant, morphologically symmetric with the upper-left creature. Body is teardrop or ovoid, covered in the same overlapping scale-plate pattern in diagonal rows. The aperture faces lower-left, and a prominent tapered 'beak' or 'snout' projection extends from the creature's anterior-left edge, angling down-left toward the center of the folio — this projection is the visual element most likely responsible for the <-> bisection at f86v4.5, as it intrudes into the text region between the two creature bodies. Blue-grey pigment accents are present on the upper scale nodes, matching the upper-left creature. A faint wash of grey or aged vellum staining is visible behind the figure, possibly a deliberate background tone or foxing. The tail base fans outward below in curved lines angling rightward.

color.blue_accent_touches: pale steel blue-grey, ~#6A8FA0 on upper scale tips
color.beak_projection: same brown ink, slightly heavier line weight, ~#7A5030

upper_center_text_medallion.description: The functional oval text zone between and below the two upper creatures, where the four @Cc-type lines of text (f86v4.1–4.4) are inscribed. This is not a drawn geometric circle but an organic negative space defined by the two creature bodies flanking it and the paragraph text below. The script here is exceptionally dense — each of the four lines contains 30–50 Voynich words — suggesting the scribe concentrated information into this central zone deliberately. The text lines are arranged horizontally and run from approximately x=240 to x=780 at the center of the page, at y positions 65–190 normalized. Parchment background: warm cream ~#E2CC95.

color.text_ink: dark brown-black, ~#2A1E0E — densest ink on the folio, well-preserved

central_sketch_zone.description: A lightly sketched, under-developed illustration zone in the center of the folio, occupying the space between the upper text block and the lower creature figures. The sketch appears to show one or two elongated organic shapes (possibly leaf pods, larval forms, or coiled botanical elements) at oblique angles, rendered in very faint, thin ink lines that may be preliminary underdrawing never completed in final ink. The lines are too faint to assign confident morphological interpretation. Some straight hatched lines cross the zone diagonally, which may be structural (scaffold lines) or representational. This zone is largely text-free, representing an 'active illustration space' reserved by the scribe.

color.sketch_lines: very faint warm grey-brown, ~#C0B090 — possibly diluted ink or faded graphite
color.background: parchment cream, ~#E2CC95, cleanest area of the page

lower_left_creature.description: A large zoomorphic or biological figure in the lower-left quadrant, the primary visual anchor for the f86v3 text bisections. The body is elongated and roughly cylindrical, tapering at both ends. The exterior is covered in overlapping scale-plates or lobed segments arranged in regular transverse bands — each band contains 5–8 individual scale units. The scale rendering is more regular and geometric than the upper creatures, suggesting a different organism type. A distinct band of blue-grey pigment (~#5A8090) crosses the mid-body diagonally, approximately 3–4 scale rows wide, creating a vivid accent stripe. The upper end of the figure features a slightly open aperture or 'mouth' rim. The lower end fans into a ruffled, lobed base or foot structure. The creature's horizontal body axis, at approximately y=810–840 normalized, is the physical element that bisects the text lines f86v3.15, 3.16, and 3.18.

color.blue_accent_band: steel blue-grey, ~#5A8090, covering approximately 3–4 transverse scale rows at mid-body

lower_right_creature.description: A large zoomorphic figure in the lower-right quadrant, the symmetric counterpart to the lower-left creature. Morphologically identical: elongated cylindrical body with transverse rows of overlapping scale-plates, blue-grey accent band at mid-body, ruffled lobe base, and aperture at the upper end. The aperture here faces upper-left, mirroring the lower-left creature's orientation. This figure appears slightly more complete and fully inked than the lower-left one, with denser scale detail in the upper body section. No text bisection events are associated with this creature — the surrounding text wraps around it rather than being interrupted by it.

lower_center_small_figure.description: A smaller organic figure in the lower-center of the folio, between the two large lower creatures. It appears as a narrow-necked vessel or bulb form with a rounded top, connected below by a thin curved stem-like line to a small cluster of round dots or pearls (possibly representing berries, eggs, or seeds). The rendering is lighter and less finished than the larger creatures. This figure occupies an isolated text-free zone between the two text columns (f86v5 left column and f86v3 lower block).

color.outline: light warm brown ink, ~#A07848 — thinner, lighter line weight than larger creatures

right_margin_text_column.description: The f86v6 text block (45 lines, @P0/+P0) runs along the entire right margin of the folio, written at 90° rotation — the text reads vertically when the folio is held normally, going from bottom to top of the column (i.e., the scribe rotated the manuscript to write normally, producing lines that appear as right-margin columns when the page is viewed right-side-up). Lines are densely packed with minimal inter-line spacing (~12–14 normalized units). The column spans the full height of the folio from approximately y=30 to y=720, with a constant x-band of approximately x=760–970. Some lines extend slightly further left where illustration elements create space. The ink is well-preserved dark brown-black.

left_margin_text_column.description: The f86v5 text block (39 lines, @P0/+Pr) runs along the left margin of the folio, also at 90° rotation — reading from top to bottom of the column when the page is viewed normally (opposite rotation from the right column). Lines span from approximately y=45 to y=720. The column occupies x=28–200. Some lines are shortened where the upper-left and lower-left creature illustrations intrude into the text zone. The terminal line (f86v5.39, +Pr) is notably short, indicating the paragraph end. Ink is the same dark brown-black as other text blocks.

lower_inverted_text_block.description: The f86v3 text block (36 lines) at the bottom of the folio, written in standard Voynich horizontal orientation but physically inverted relative to the top of the page — i.e., this block is upside-down when the folio is read from the top. This is consistent with the folio being written from both ends (recto and verso of a bifolio) or the manuscript being flipped. The block has two sub-sections: @Pb lines (3.1–3.14 and 3.23–3.36) forming bracket-style paragraph openings, and @P0/+P0 lines (3.15–3.22) in between containing the three bisection events. Lines run from approximately y=840 to y=998.

color.text_ink: dark brown-black, ~#2A1E0E, consistent with upper text blocks
color.background: slightly more yellowed parchment at bottom edge, ~#D8C080

isolated_zones.status: Partially text-free — creature body is illustration-only, but left margin text column (f86v5) runs adjacent to its right edge
isolated_zones.description: The upper-left creature body itself is a text-free illustration zone from approximately x=18–340, y=10–270. The left margin text column (f86v5) begins at x=22 but the creature's right extent (~x=340) pushes into what would normally be the text column's right boundary, causing line-length compression in f86v5 lines 3.9–3.10. The creature's interior surface — its scale body — is entirely free of Voynich text; no glyphs overlap with the illustration body. Color: warm brown ink outline on parchment cream interior, with ~8–12 pale blue accent dots on upper scale tips.

isolated_zones.status: Partially text-free — creature body is illustration-only; beak projection directly causes the f86v4.5 bisection
isolated_zones.description: The upper-right creature body (x=610–980, y=10–300) is an illustration-only zone. No text is written on the creature's body interior. The beak/snout projection extending lower-left from the creature is the active bisecting element for line f86v4.5, with the gap in that line (x≈479–538) corresponding exactly to the projection's crossing of the text baseline. The right margin text column (f86v6) runs to the right of and below this creature, beginning at approximately y=28.

isolated_zones.status: Intentionally text-free — reserved illustration space, underdeveloped
isolated_zones.description: The center of the folio (x=180–680, y=415–660) is entirely text-free. No Voynich text appears in this zone across any of the four text blocks. The zone contains only faint underdrawing or lightly sketched forms. This represents either an intended illustration space left incomplete, a deliberate compositional pause between the upper text zone and lower creature zone, or a sketch that was planned but abandoned. The negative space here is structurally significant — it separates the upper text cluster (f86v4) from the lower figure group and lower text blocks.

isolated_zones.status: Intentionally bisected — creature body horizontally traverses the f86v3 text zone, causing three <-> bisection events
isolated_zones.description: The lower-left creature (x=58–395, y=745–990) is the most structurally active illustration element on the folio in terms of text interaction. Its mid-body tube crosses the f86v3 text zone at y=900–985 (normalized), producing bisections at lines 3.15, 3.16, and 3.18. The gaps in those three lines (each approximately 139–146 normalized units wide) define the creature's body width at those cross-sections. The creature's scale-body interior is text-free; text resumes on both sides of the body. The blue-grey accent band (~#5A8090) crossing the creature's mid-body is visible within the bisection gap zone and serves as a visual confirmation of the creature's body position. The creature's frilled/lobed base at y=960–990 is also text-free.

isolated_zones.status: Completely text-free — surrounded by but not crossed by any text block
isolated_zones.description: The lower-right creature (x=575–945, y=730–990) is an entirely text-free illustration zone. Unlike the lower-left creature, no text bisections occur here — the right margin column (f86v6) runs to its right and above, and the lower inverted text block (f86v3) does not extend far enough right to be interrupted by this figure. The creature is surrounded by negative space on three sides (right, bottom, center-left). Its blue-grey accent band and scale-body interior are text-free throughout.

isolated_zones.status: Completely text-free — occupies a natural gap between left column, right column, and lower text blocks
isolated_zones.description: The small lower-center figure (x=398–560, y=700–830) occupies an isolated text-free island between the three surrounding text blocks. The left margin column (f86v5) ends before reaching this x-zone; the right margin column (f86v6) begins after; the lower inverted block (f86v3) does not reach this y-zone. The result is a naturally isolated pocket where the small organism figure sits without any text interaction whatsoever. This negative space isolation may be deliberate — the scribe may have positioned this small figure in a gap that was too narrow for a full text block.
